decisions.rationale: dataset.duplicate_row_rate is 0.0 across row_count 3322, so no exact-duplicate row removal is needed.
tailnum has distinct_count 3322 equal to row_count 3322 with null_rate 0.0, so it alone identifies one row per aircraft registry entry.
year has null_count 70 (null_rate 0.021072); nulls are retained rather than imputed per the publisher's NA convention noted in operator context.
speed has null_count 3299 (null_rate 0.993076), making it sparsely populated; it is retained nullable rather than dropped since the remaining values are valid cruising speeds.
_airbyte_raw_id, _airbyte_extracted_at, and _airbyte_meta are all flagged is_airbyte_metadata true and carry no business meaning.
operator context specifies measures are named with a unit suffix, and speed is documented as average cruising speed in mph, hence speed_mph.
engine (6 categorical values like Turbo-fan, Reciprocating) is renamed to engine_type to avoid confusion with the numeric engines count column.
year, engines, seats, and speed all land as DECIMAL(38,9) but every sampled or distinct value is integral, so each is cast to INTEGER.

purpose: This silver table provides a cleaned registry of aircraft (one row per tail number) drawn from the FAA's 2014 release as reduced to tail numbers seen in the 2013 NYC flights dataset, feeding downstream joins from flight records to aircraft characteristics such as manufacturer, model, engine type, and capacity.
usage: Join on tailnum to enrich flight-level records with aircraft attributes; treat year_manufactured and speed_mph as optionally null and filter or coalesce them explicitly before aggregation, since speed_mph is populated for under 1% of rows.
limitations: speed_mph is populated for only about 0.7% of rows (null_rate 0.993076) and should not be relied on for broad analysis; year is missing for about 2.1% of rows; American Airlines and Envoy Air aircraft are absent from this registry because those carriers reported fleet numbers rather than tail numbers, per operator context.
